authority.note: THE SPINE OBJECT of The Room It Was Made In. Its whole job is to be ORDINARY and SPECIFIC: the book's argument is that a made thing comes out like the room it was made in, which only lands if the room looks like a real place people work rather than a temple or a set. Chain `night` off `wide` so it is unmistakably the same room. BOTH PLATES FIRST ROLL 2026-07-28; the chain held (same windows, shelf, layout, and the same jacket over the same chair in both states). DRESSING REWRITTEN 2026-07-28 after the first render batch: it previously enumerated 'TWO STATES. wide: ... night: ...', and because resolve_setting() feeds contract.dressing directly into the prompt, that read as a spec for two pictures. Twelve of twenty-eight spreads came back as stacked day/night diptychs. Same class as the multi-state visual-metaphor bug, but on a SETTING via contract.dressing rather than prose.rules. Per-state light now lives in each spread's scene text, and the dressing carries an explicit one-moment-in-time instruction.

contract.map: THE ROOM: one long working room in an ordinary building, the kind a small company grows into rather than commissions. Plain desks pushed together in irregular clusters, mismatched chairs, monitors, laptops, a whiteboard with half-erased diagrams, printouts taped to a wall, mugs, a shelf of well-used books, cables. Big plain windows down one side. No open-plan tech-campus gloss, no branding, no slogans on the walls, no neon, no glass conference boxes.
contract.blocking: The camera is INSIDE the room at standing or seated eye height, never a lobby shot and never an architectural exterior. The clusters of desks give it depth. People are ordinary in scale and are never arranged to face a leader; if anyone is speaking, the group is loose around them rather than seated in rows.
contract.dressing: The room is LIVED-IN and a little untidy, with evidence of people everywhere whether or not anyone is in frame: a jacket over a chair back, an open notebook, a half-drunk mug, printouts curling where they are taped up, mismatched chairs pushed at angles. It is NEVER sterile, NEVER a showroom, and NEVER lit dramatically; the light is only ever whatever the room actually has at that hour. RENDER EXACTLY ONE MOMENT IN TIME: one single continuous scene at one time of day, filling the whole frame. Do NOT divide the image, do NOT stack a daytime version above a night version, do NOT show the room twice, and do NOT produce a before-and-after or side-by-side comparison of any kind.
contract.scale: One long room, human-scaled, low ceiling rather than an atrium. It should feel like somewhere about a hundred people could work, not a headquarters.

prose.rules: The room is the argument, so it must never be aspirational. Every temptation to make it impressive is a temptation to break the book: no soaring ceilings, no branded wall, no dramatic lighting, no rows of identical monitors. It is a good ordinary room where careful people work, and the whole thesis is that THAT is where a character comes from.
